name: cctp_bridging
description: Missing reentrancy protection in CCTP V2 hook receiver contracts after USDC mint
question: The source file in `source` defines a contract that receives CCTP V2 minted USDC and executes hook calldata (e.g., logic invoked after MessageTransmitter.receiveMessage/receiveMessageWithCaller delivers a mint plus hookData) that performs external calls such as approvals, transfers, or calls into a vault/DEX using that hook data, but the function executing the hook lacks a reentrancy guard (no nonReentrant modifier or mutex) and updates or relies on contract state after the external call, allowing an attacker to reenter and manipulate balances or state during hook execution.
criteria: Function processes hookData/calldata delivered alongside a CCTP mint (e.g., from depositForBurnWithHook or a destination hook receiver)
Function makes an external call (transfer, approve, low-level call, or call to vault/DEX) using the decoded hook data
No nonReentrant modifier, reentrancy guard, or mutex flag protects the hook-executing function
State variables (balances, accounting, minted amounts) are read or written after the external call
No check-effects-interactions ordering enforced around the hook execution
